g.text: SEMICONDUCTOR DIODE PHYSICS, MODELS & DC OPERATING POINT ENGINE
Comprehensive Lattice Kinetics, Shockley V-I Mechanics, Assumed States 4-Step Engine & Logic Gates
GATE 2027 TITAN SUITE
FIGURE 1 • 4K VECTOR
1. Semiconductor Lattice, Doping & Carrier Statistics
• Silicon Crystal Lattice: Diamond cubic structure with 4 valence electrons forming covalent bonds.
• Thermal Generation at T > 0 K: Thermal vibration breaks bonds → creates free e⁻ and hole pairs.
Intrinsic Carrier Concentration: n_i² = B · T³ · exp(-E_g / k T) (at 300K, n_i ≈ 1.5×10¹⁰ cm⁻³ in Si)
• Extrinsic Semiconductors & Mass Action Law (n · p = n_i²):
N-Type: Group V (P, As, Sb) → Donors (N_D⁺). Majority: e⁻ (n_n ≈ N_D), Minority: holes (p_n = n_i² / N_D)
P-Type: Group III (B, Ga, In) → Acceptors (N_A⁻). Majority: holes (p_p ≈ N_A), Minority: e⁻ (n_p = n_i² / N_A)
• Charge Neutrality: q(N_D⁺ + p) = q(N_A⁻ + n) ⇒ Total crystal remains strictly electrically neutral!
★ Trap 01: Doping increases conductivity exponentially but does NOT give net static electric charge.
2. PN Junction Electrostatics & Built-In Potential (V₀)
• Depletion Region Formation: Diffusion leaves uncompensated donor (N_D⁺) & acceptor (N_A⁻) space-charge ions.
Built-In Potential: V₀ = V_T · ln((N_A · N_D) / n_i²) where V_T = k T / q ≈ 26 mV at 300 K
• Typical Values: V₀ ≈ 0.7 V for Silicon; V₀ ≈ 0.3 V for Germanium.
• Depletion Width: W = √[ (2 ε / q) · (1/N_A + 1/N_D) · (V₀ - V_D) ]
- Asymmetric Junction: W penetrates predominantly into LIGHTLY doped side (W_p N_A = W_n N_D).
• Biasing Regimes:
- Forward Bias (V_D > 0): Barrier lowered to (V₀ - V_D), depletion width thins, large diffusion current.
- Reverse Bias (V_D < 0): Barrier widened to (V₀ + |V_R|), depletion width expands, negligible drift current I_s.
★ Vital Rule: Built-in potential V₀ CANNOT be measured by a standard voltmeter across diode terminals!
3. Shockley Diode V-I Kinetics & Temperature Sensitivity
I_D = I_s · [ exp( V_D / (η · V_T) ) - 1 ]
• I_s (Reverse Saturation Current): Thermally generated minority carrier drift current.
- Temperature Dependency: I_s DOUBLES for every 10°C temperature rise in Si (approx 7%/°C rise).
- Magnitude Comparison: I_s ≈ 1 pA - 1 nA in Silicon; I_s ≈ 1 µA in Germanium (1000× larger!).
• Ideality Factor η: η = 1 for Ge; η = 1 (high currents) and η = 2 (low currents) for Si.
• Forward Voltage Tempco: (d V_D / d T) |_(I_D=const) ≈ -2.5 mV/°C (for Si at 300K).
• Voltage Step for 10× Current Multiplier (One Decade):
ΔV_D = 2.3 · η · V_T ≈ 60 mV (for η = 1 at 300 K)
Every 60 mV increase in forward bias multiplies the forward current by a full decade (10×)!
4. Diode Equivalent Models Hierarchy
• Model 1: Ideal Diode (Lossless Switch)
- Forward: Short circuit (V_D = 0 V, I_D > 0). Reverse: Open circuit (I_D = 0 A, V_D < 0).
• Model 2: Practical Diode (Offset Battery Model)
- Forward: Constant DC drop V_γ = 0.7 V (Si) / 0.3 V (Ge). Reverse: Open circuit.
• Model 3: Piecewise Linear Model (Offset + Forward Bulk Resistance)
- Forward: V_D = V_γ + I_D · r_f where r_f = dynamic forward resistance (10 Ω - 50 Ω).
• Model 4: Small-Signal AC Incremental Model
- Dynamic AC resistance r_d = η V_T / I_DQ in parallel with diffusion/transition capacitance.
★ Selection Criterion: Use Model 1 if supply V_s >> 10 V; use Model 2/3 when V_s is close to 0.7 V.
5. Method of Assumed States (4-Step Engine)
STEP 1: Formulate Initial Diode State Hypothesis
• Inspect supply polarities. If cathode is connected to high positive potential, assume OFF.
• If anode is connected to high positive potential, assume ON.
For N diodes, there are 2^N possible permutation states.
STEP 2: Substitute Respective Circuit Models
• For assumed ON diode: Replace with short-circuit (ideal) or 0.7 V battery (anode positive).
• For assumed OFF diode: Replace with open-circuit.
The non-linear circuit is transformed into a pure linear resistive network!
STEP 3: Solve Linear Network via KVL / KCL
• Calculate the forward branch current I_D for all diodes assumed ON.
• Calculate the open-circuit anode-to-cathode voltage V_D = V_A - V_K for all diodes assumed OFF.
Use standard nodal analysis or mesh analysis.
STEP 4: Verify Consistency Criteria
✓ If assumed ON: Must satisfy I_D > 0 (current flows from Anode to Cathode)
✓ If assumed OFF: Must satisfy V_D < 0 (ideal) or V_D < V_γ (practical)
✗ Contradiction Rule: If ANY diode violates its criterion, assumption is INVALID!
Flip the state of the violating diode and re-execute Steps 2 through 4.
★ High-Yield Parallel Diode Contention Rule:
When diodes with different cut-in voltages (e.g. Ge 0.3V vs Si 0.7V) are in parallel with common anode,
the diode with LOWER cut-in voltage turns ON first, clamping anode and keeping the other OFF!
6. DC Load Line & Operating Point (Q-Point)
• Series Diode-Resistor Circuit: V_S = I_D · R_L + V_D
Load Line Equation: I_D = - (1 / R_L) · V_D + (V_S / R_L)
• Two Key Intercepts:
- Voltage Axis Intercept (I_D = 0): V_D = V_S (Open-circuit voltage)
- Current Axis Intercept (V_D = 0): I_D = V_S / R_L (Short-circuit current)
• Slope of DC Load Line: m = - 1 / R_L (Determined strictly by external load resistance!)
• Quiescent Point (Q-Point): Intersection of non-linear diode V-I curve and DC load line.

★ Sensitivity Rule: Changing V_S shifts load line parallelly; changing R_L pivots load line around V_S.
7. Classic Multi-Diode Logic Topologies
Case A: Diode OR Logic Gate (Common Cathode)
• Anodes connected to inputs V₁, V₂; cathodes tied together to ground via pull-down resistor R.
• Operation: V_o = max(V₁, V₂) - V_γ. The diode with the HIGHEST input potential conducts;
its cathode potential rises, reverse-biasing and turning OFF all other parallel diodes!
Case B: Diode AND Logic Gate (Common Anode)
• Cathodes connected to inputs V₁, V₂; anodes tied together to V_CC via pull-up resistor R.
• Operation: V_o = min(V₁, V₂) + V_γ. The diode with the LOWEST input potential conducts;
pulling anode potential down, which reverse-biases and turns OFF all other parallel diodes!
Case C: Back-to-Back Series Opposing Diodes
• Diode D₁ (anode left) and D₂ (cathode left) in series with supply V_S.
• No matter the polarity of V_S, one diode is forward-biased and the other is reverse-biased.
• Current is strictly limited to reverse saturation current I_s: I ≈ I_s!
Almost the ENTIRE applied voltage V_S drops across the reverse-biased diode.
★ GATE Master Rule for Diode Networks:
Always test the most extreme voltage node first (highest positive or most negative) to identify the primary conducting branch.
